name: The Royal Match
about: The council says the crown needs an heir, and two great houses each offer a daughter to wed. Pick one and the other is shamed. Pick neither and both turn on you. Then comes the birth, and being royal doesn't make it any safer.
title: The Royal Match

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: The small council says out loud what the whole realm is whispering. The crown has no heir of the King's own blood, and a throne with no heir is a prize for anyone. Two houses answer at once.

court.text: {first} of {first.house} and {second} of {second.house} stand on either side of the hall, each holding a portrait. "{firstChild} is of age, Your Grace." "So is {secondChild}, and her blood is better."

options.label: Wed {firstChild} of {first.house}
options.result: The banns are read for the King and {firstChild}. {second} walks out of the hall before they finish.

options.label: Wed {secondChild} of {second.house}
options.result: The banns are read for the King and {secondChild}. {first} smiles too wide and says nothing.

options.label: Wait, and choose later
options.hint: both houses wait, but not for long
options.result: The portraits go in a cupboard. Both houses start looking for other friends.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: {second.house} wears grey to the royal wedding. At the feast {second} drinks to the bride's health, and to every child she may never have.

court.text: {second}: "My house was passed over in front of the whole realm, Your Grace. Words won't fix that."

options.label: Make amends with a gift and a council seat (300 gold)
options.result: {second} takes the council seat and the gold, and bows exactly as low as the law requires, and no lower.

options.label: Refuse to make amends
options.result: The King offers nothing. {second} rides home, and {second.his} letters go out to every enemy of {first.house}.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: {first.house} sends a wedding gift: a fine silver cradle with a crack down the middle.

court.text: {first}: "You chose {second.house}, Your Grace, and the whole realm saw it. My house needs to see something in return."

options.label: Make amends with a gift and a council seat (300 gold)
options.result: {first} takes the council seat and the gold, and says the cradle was a joke.

options.label: Refuse to make amends
options.result: The King sends the cracked cradle back. {first} has it mended and keeps it on {first.his} table.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: The quarrel between {first.house} and {second.house} turns into a war. Banners go up along the border of their lands, and the King's in-laws ask him for help.

court.text: {first}: "They're burning my villages because you favoured one house over the other, Your Grace. Stand with your family, or stay out of it."

options.label: Send the royal host to help your in-laws
options.result: Royal knights ride out to fight beside the Queen's family.

options.label: Make peace between them (200 gold)
options.hint: both houses +5 · two years of truce
options.result: The King's heralds stand between the two armies until both lords are too cold to keep fighting.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: The quarrel between {second.house} and {first.house} turns into a war. Banners go up along the border of their lands, and the King's in-laws ask him for help.

court.text: {second}: "They're burning my villages because you favoured one house over the other, Your Grace. Stand with your family, or stay out of it."

options.label: Send the royal host to help your in-laws
options.result: Royal knights ride out to fight beside the Queen's family.

options.label: Make peace between them (200 gold)
options.hint: both houses +5 · two years of truce
options.result: The King's heralds stand between the two armies until both lords are too cold to keep fighting.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: Two winters pass and still no royal wedding. {first} and {second} agree on nothing, but now they're seen riding together, and the taverns say the realm will pick its own heir.

court.text: {second}: "The realm is tired of waiting, Your Grace. Choose now, or the lords will choose for you, and it won't be a bride they choose."

options.label: Wed {firstChild} of {first.house}, now
options.result: The King weds {firstChild} within the month, in a hurry and in the rain.

options.label: Wed {secondChild} of {second.house}, now
options.result: The King weds {secondChild} within the month, in a hurry and in the rain.

options.label: Refuse to be rushed
options.hint: both houses −15 · they'll pick an heir of their own
options.result: The King refuses. {first} and {second} leave together.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: At {first.seat}, {first} and {second} swear on the old stones that a King with no heir is no King. {first} marches on Kingsmere to take charge of the realm as its protector.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: {second} stops calling it a quarrel between houses. {second.His} heralds read out a new claim: the crown now serves one house only, so it has to go.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: {first} stops calling it a quarrel between houses. {first.His} heralds read out a new claim: the crown now serves one house only, so it has to go.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: The Queen is with child. The midwives come from three houses, and none of them trusts the other two. All of Kingsmere waits under the windows.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: The child is born alive, but the Queen dies before morning. {first}, her {first.father}, wants to know which midwife washed her hands and which didn't.

court.text: {first}, dressed in black: "My daughter died in your bed, Your Grace. Let my house raise the child, or hand me the midwife who killed her."

options.label: Let the Queen's family raise the heir
options.hint: {first.houseName} +25 · the heir is in their hands
options.result: The heir goes to be raised by the Queen's family. They swear the child will know its mother's face from her portraits.

options.label: Keep the heir at Kingsmere
options.result: The heir stays at Kingsmere. The Queen's father doesn't come to the naming.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: The child is born alive, but the Queen dies before morning. {second}, her {second.father}, wants to know which midwife washed her hands and which didn't.

court.text: {second}, dressed in black: "My daughter died in your bed, Your Grace. Let my house raise the child, or hand me the midwife who killed her."

options.label: Let the Queen's family raise the heir
options.hint: {second.houseName} +25 · the heir is in their hands
options.result: The heir goes to be raised by the Queen's family. They swear the child will know its mother's face from her portraits.

options.label: Keep the heir at Kingsmere
options.result: The heir stays at Kingsmere. The Queen's father doesn't come to the naming.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: One of the King's two promised brides is dead, and the other house is blamed before the body is cold.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: The bells of Kingsmere ring for a royal heir, loud and healthy. The lords who wanted the throne for themselves come to the naming and kneel to the cradle.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: The lords who wanted to choose the King's heir for him are beaten. He rules on with no Queen and no heir, and the realm stops asking.
